title: Make models.opencode real and define the bee worker agents
action: Per plan.md E4, CONTEXT.md D1/D4 and D5 (sequential dispatch accepted): make `opencode` a real key of the `models` config alongside claude and codex — today docs/config-reference.md:78-100 says any other key is SILENTLY IGNORED, which would make a models.opencode block look configured while doing nothing; find where the models map is read in packages/bee-rs and make the opencode key first-class there (tier resolution for extraction/generation/review), or, if the reader is already runtime-agnostic, prove that with a test and correct the doc's claim instead. Then write the four .opencode/agent/<name>.md worker definitions mirroring .claude/agents/bee-{build,gather,extract,review}.md: frontmatter description + mode: subagent + permission (read-only agents must not be able to write) + a model pinned from the matching models.opencode tier, prompt bodies carrying the same worker contract. Pinning the model per agent is what makes a wrong-tier dispatch unrepresentable on OpenCode (the structural half of the model-guard mapping). Do not touch .opencode/plugins/bee-guard.ts or discovery.md — other cells own them; record your evidence in the commit body and cell outcome.

truths: A models.opencode block is honored by the tier reader, or the doc's silently-ignored claim is corrected with a test proving the reader is runtime-agnostic
Each of the four agent files pins a model from its matching tier and sets mode: subagent
Read-only agents (gather, extract, review) cannot write, per their permission frontmatter
No edits land in bee-guard.ts or discovery.md
